Without this, lex_from / scan_decimal recursive calls compile as regular
call_indirect; long inputs trap "call stack exhausted". With it, fn /
lambda / handler-arm bodies are walked top-down for structural tail
position (LIf branches, LBlock last stmt, LMatch arm bodies); LCall in
tail rewrites to LTailCall (309) which emit_call.wat:264 already lowers
to return_call_indirect.

Bootstrap: $lower_mark_tail in walk_call.wat; called from
walk_stmt.wat (FnStmt body), walk_compound.wat (lambda body),
walk_handle.wat (handler arm body × 2 call paths). Wheel-side mirror
in src/lower.mn (mark_tail + 4 call sites; LMatch arms rebuild via
mark_tail_arms; LIf/LBlock list-tails mutate in place via list_set).

Empirical: mentl2 = m1-compiled wheel was trapping at frame 5+ with
massive lex_from self-recursion (5+ identical addresses 0x28eb7).
Post-landing, mentl2 runs cleanly to completion on tiny input (0 bytes
output is the orthogonal perform wat_emit fallthrough — task #123).

LRegion / LHandleWith / LFeedback bodies deliberately do NOT propagate
tail (handler-cleanup / region-exit / feedback-continuation runs after
the body's last expression — a tail call would skip surrounding
control-flow).

Eight interrogations: tail-position is structural property of the
LowExpr graph (Graph), lower walks deriving it (Handler), |> chain's
rightmost stage IS tail (Verb), no row change (Row/Ownership/Refinement),
compile-time guarantee (Gradient), Reason chain reads "tail because
terminal expression of fn-body / branch-of-tail-LIf / arm-of-tail-LMatch
/ last-stmt-of-tail-LBlock" (Reason).

Drift refused: 1 (no vtable — direct constructor swap), 6 (LCall and
LTailCall already exist as distinct ADT variants — no flag-as-int),
8 (no mode-int), 9 (lands whole bootstrap+wheel together; not deferred
"wheel later").

Closes task #124. Wheel-source LIf-branches mutate in place, LMatch
arms rebuild — mirror of bootstrap's Ω.3 buffer-counter discipline at
arm-tuple granularity.
mentl/2562233:
Per SYNTAX.md `_` is the wildcard pattern — the canonical no-binding
sentinel. When multiple `_` params appear in the same fn signature
(e.g., `fn f(_, _, x) = ...`), lower extracts each as the literal
name "_"; emit produces `(param $_ i32)` twice; wat2wasm rejects.

Substrate fix per the eight interrogations / ULTIMATE form:
- Graph: param's name from lower; LPWild flattened to "_"
- Refinement: Verify(uniqueness) — restored
- Drift refused: 6 (special-case) — wildcard "_" IS the substrate-
  defined no-binding sentinel; recognizing it is the canonical
  projection, not drift. The $i suffix derives from existing graph
  data (param index), not parallel state.

The substrate-honest form would be anonymous WAT param `(param i32)`
since the wildcard has no body reference (verified: 0 `(local.get $_)`
sites in wheel-out). Synth-name `_<i>` is equivalent in effect (no
collision; never referenced) and simpler to retrofit at the emit
site without restructuring the param-emit format string set.

Empirical:
  Pre:  619 errors / 13 redef of parameter
  Post: 608 errors / 2 redef of parameter (-11; -85%)
  Cumulative: 3708 → 608 (-83.6%) in 8 substrate moves.

Residual 2 redefs are `$e` and `$q` — actual wheel-source double-
param-name typos (not seed substrate). Wheel-source completeness,
not L1-blocker substrate.

Eight interrogations:
  1. Graph?     param's name string from lower; "_" matches by byte
                check (str_len==1, byte_at(0)==0x5F).
  2. Handler?   $emit_fn_body's param-emit loop; @resume=OneShot.
  3. Verb?      |> sequential walk per param.
  4. Row?       +EmitMemory -Input -Mutate Pure.
  5. Ownership? Wildcards have no binding to consume/borrow.
  6. Refinement? Verify(uniqueness); closed by per-param-index
                synth-name on the wildcard sentinel.
  7. Gradient?  N/A — structural.
  8. Reason?    Wildcards have no Reason chain.

noodles/2586efa:
The global dice maximized timbre and wasted the music: every roll was the
same drummer, the same bass player, and a dry room under a different
synth. A vibe now rolls once per song: a weighted groove archetype
(four-floor, backbeat, halftime, 2-step via euclid, minimal — each owning
its kick placement, hat grid, velocity personality, tempo band, and pocket
range), weighted bass behaviors, a melody built as a repeated-and-varied
motif instead of uniform scatter, weighted harmony families with rolled
length (1/2/4 bars, timeline placement floored at 4 bars so a short
progression loops instead of exporting silence), registers rolled once so
the ✨b variation scene (60% of rolls) stays in the A scene's octave, a
kit hire (60%, groove-matched), and spice at low rates (harmonyOct 15%, a
12-step polymeter lane 10%). About a third of rolls arrive wet — verb on
pad and lead, echo on lead, never bass or drums — and the dice owns the
sends: a dry roll resets them, faders/pan/mutes stay the player's
(DECISIONS D9).

The vibe carries only rolled values; archetype constants stay in the
GROOVES table and derive from the groove name, so the full vibe persists
on the song and the session Magic button generates in the same vibe
instead of rolling a fresh one at the wrong tempo. Receipts: 24-roll
variety (all grooves and kits appear, no degenerate rolls — every roll
keeps a kick, a bassline, three melody notes), calibrate dice cohesion
holds at 1.9 dB master spread with wet rolls in play, smoke green with
the 1-2 scene contract.
